title: After a Suspected Chemical Attack, a Syrian Tells His Story

sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.zh: 我负责报道《纽约时报》每日简讯Dealbook的

sentences.zh: 商业与政策新闻。

sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市Dealbook峰会的现场采访商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的几位领袖，其中包括J.D.

sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 今天，美国

sentences.en: says that the suspected chemical weapons attack on the rebel-held town of Douma earlier this month was part of a military push by the Syrian government to break the will
sentences.zh: 表示，本月早些时候对反叛武装控制的杜马镇疑似化武袭击，是叙利亚政府旨在粉碎

sentences.en: of the people still living there.
sentences.zh: 当地居民意志的军事进攻的一部分。

sentences.en: We speak to one of them.
sentences.zh: 我们采访了其中的一位居民。

sentences.en: It's Monday, April 23rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是4月23日，星期一。

sentences.en: The first responders and the firefighters can't get to the fires around the area because of the heavy shilling.
sentences.zh: 由于猛烈的炮击，急救人员和消防员无法进入周边地区灭火。

sentences.en: It's very dangerous to roam around in the streets.
sentences.zh: 在街上游荡非常危险。

sentences.en: Warplanes, Russian warplanes, the regime's airstrikes.
sentences.zh: 战机，俄罗斯战机，政权的发动空袭。

sentences.en: The shilling hasn't stopped in essence.
sentences.zh: 炮击基本上没有停过。

sentences.en: It's been going on for about 24 hours.
sentences.zh: 这种情况已经持续了大约24小时。

sentences.en: And I don't think that the situation, that the actual picture is getting out there.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为真实的情况并没有传达出去。

sentences.en: This is a big problem.
sentences.zh: 这是一个大问题。

sentences.en: Mahmoud Wadwani grew up in Douma.
sentences.zh: 马哈茂德·瓦德瓦尼在杜马长大。

sentences.en: Two weeks ago, when government forces moved to retake the city.
sentences.zh: 两周前，当政府军开始重新夺回这座城市时。

sentences.en: Mahmoud was there.
sentences.zh: 马哈茂德就在那里。

sentences.en: Yeah, at that time, the regime was launching a very strong assault and heavy shilling on Douma city.
sentences.zh: 是的，当时政权对杜马市发动了非常猛烈的进攻和密集的炮击。

sentences.en: They started the shilling with airstrikes and artillery, and it got escalated gradually.
sentences.zh: 他们从空袭和炮击开始，并且逐渐升级。

sentences.en: My house got hit.
sentences.zh: 我的房子被击中了。

sentences.en: We were in the basement, and my house got hit with a land-to-land missile.
sentences.zh: 我们当时在地下室，然后我家的房子被地对地导弹击中了。

sentences.en: We heard the noise, and the building got shot for a second or something.
sentences.zh: 我们听到了巨响，整栋建筑震动了一秒钟左右。

sentences.en: Can I ask you, what was it like when your house was hit with this missile?
sentences.zh: 请问，当你的房子被这枚导弹击中时，那是什么感觉？

sentences.en: Did you hear it coming?
sentences.zh: 你听到它飞过来了吗？

sentences.en: How much warning did you have?
sentences.zh: 你有多少时间的预警？

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: No, no time.
sentences.zh: 没有，根本没有时间。

sentences.en: We were in the basement, like I said, so the missile hit just three floors above us, if that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，我们当时在地下室，所以导弹正好击中了我们头顶上方三层楼，如果这么说能理解的话。

sentences.en: We tried to put out the fire, but we were helpless.
sentences.zh: 我们试图灭火，但我们无能为力。

sentences.en: We couldn't do anything.
sentences.zh: 我们什么也做不了。

sentences.en: We tried to control the fire and, you know, trap it in one room or something, but that failed to, when a fire starts, there is no firefighters to put it out.
sentences.zh: 我们试图控制火势，你知道的，把它困在一个房间里什么的，但这也失败了，火灾一旦发生，就没有消防员来扑灭它。

sentences.en: So it kind of just spreads to other areas, nearby apartments and such things.
sentences.zh: 所以它就蔓延到了其他地方，比如附近的公寓之类的。

sentences.en: At that night, I actually was standing on the rubble of my own house.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上，我其实正站在自己家废墟的瓦砾上。

sentences.en: It was burned down that night.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上它被烧成了平地。

sentences.en: When I went out of the basement, I saw a big amount of destruction, something we did not have in our minds, something we could not have imagined.
sentences.zh: 当我走出地下室时，我看到了大量的破坏，这是我们做梦也没想到、根本无法想象的景象。

sentences.en: The connections were cut off the city by the regime, so I was afraid that we might be slaughtered without anyone knowing what's happening.
sentences.zh: 政权切断了该市的通讯，所以我担心我们可能会在没人知道发生了什么的情况下被屠杀。

sentences.en: So I started recording what's happening.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始记录发生的事情。

sentences.en: I started recording the destruction and the fires that were around me.
sentences.zh: 我开始记录周围的破坏和火灾。

sentences.en: People are bombing water manually.
sentences.zh: 人们在人工灭火。

sentences.en: Moving on the streets is now very dangerous.
sentences.zh: 现在在街上走动非常危险。

sentences.en: So you have to run to the nearest basement.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须跑向最近的地下室。

sentences.en: Can you tell me about Duma as you remember it before all this, when you were growing up there?
sentences.zh: 能跟我讲讲你记忆中这一切发生之前的杜马吗？就是你在这里长大时的样子。

sentences.en: Before the revolution started, what I remember from back then was just going to school and playing on the field and things like that.
sentences.zh: 在革命爆发之前，我记忆中的那个时期就是上学、在球场上踢球之类的事情。

sentences.en: And there was a park right outside our building.
sentences.zh: 我们大楼外面正好有一个公园。

sentences.en: And I remember how nice the people were to each other, how beautiful it was to play a little football, for example.
sentences.zh: 我记得人们对彼此多好，踢会儿足球是多么美好的一件事，比如说。

sentences.en: So you play soccer?
sentences.zh: 所以你踢足球？

sentences.en: Yeah, back then.
sentences.zh: 对，那时候踢。

sentences.en: Were you good at it?
sentences.zh: 你踢得好吗？

sentences.en: Not really.
sentences.zh: 一般般。

sentences.en: But it was a very enjoyable game for me.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说这是一项非常快乐的运动。

sentences.en: Running around and the team playing, I really enjoyed that.
sentences.zh: 四处奔跑和团队配合，我真的很享受。

sentences.en: So I wasn't the best, but I did okay.
sentences.zh: 所以我不是最好的，但我踢得还行。

sentences.en: When was the last time you were able to go out into a park?
sentences.zh: 你上一次去公园是什么时候？

sentences.en: That was a long, long time ago.
sentences.zh: 那是很久很久以前了。

sentences.en: When did things start to change in Duma?
sentences.zh: 杜马是什么时候开始发生变化的？

sentences.en: Duma participated in the demonstration since the beginning.
sentences.zh: 杜马从一开始就参与了游行示威。

sentences.en: I think it was about 15 of
sentences.zh: 我想大概是

sentences.en: April, that's what I think, in 2011.
sentences.zh: 4月15日吧，我记得是2011年。

sentences.en: Yeah, it felt hopeful.
sentences.zh: 是的，当时感觉充满了希望。

sentences.en: And this is what many of us now know as the Arab Spring.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们现在许多人所知道的阿拉伯之春。

sentences.en: That was happening in Duma in 2011.
sentences.zh: 2011年那正在杜马发生。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: How old were you in 2011 when these protests were starting?
sentences.zh: 2011年这些抗议活动开始时你多大？

sentences.en: So did you participate in them, or were you just watching them from home?
sentences.zh: 那你参加了吗，还是只是在家看着？

sentences.en: Yeah, I participated.
sentences.zh: 是的，我参加了。

sentences.en: After the first violent attack that happened on the civilians in these demonstrations, an act of violence that killed, as I remember, about 11 of Duma's own people.
sentences.zh: 在这些示威活动中发生针对平民的第一次暴力袭击之后，那次暴力行动据我记杀死大约11名杜马本地人。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: That's when I knew exactly that I have to participate in these peaceful acts to act and demand for human rights.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，我清楚地知道我必须参与到这些和平行动中去，行动起来争取人权。

sentences.en: Did the protests continue despite the attacks?
sentences.zh: 尽管遭到袭击，抗议活动仍在继续吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It continued for a long time.
sentences.zh: 持续了很长时间。

sentences.en: The regime escalated everything into a war.
sentences.zh: 政权把一切都升级为了一场战争。

sentences.en: What would be a typical day for you once the rebellion was underway and you were participating in it?
sentences.zh: 一旦起义全面展开并且你参与其中，你典型的一天是怎么度过的？

sentences.en: What was it like?
sentences.zh: 那是什么样的？

sentences.en: My day routine was to go to school and after school, I'd ask my friends about the place of
sentences.zh: 我的日常就是去上学，放学后，我会向朋友们打听

sentences.en: today's demonstration, where it will be.
sentences.zh: 今天的示威地点在哪里。

sentences.en: And then if anything is asked of me, like if I have to film the demonstration, you know, if no one is filming the demonstration, and gather with the other activists and start the
sentences.zh: 然后如果有人让我做什么，比如让我拍摄示威活动，你知道的，如果没有人拍摄示威活动，就和其他激进分子汇合并开始

sentences.en: demonstration, that's all.
sentences.zh: 游行，就是这样。

sentences.en: Then the security forces would come and sometimes start shooting, sometimes just throw smoke grenades.
sentences.zh: 然后安全部队就会来，有时开始开枪，有时只是投掷催泪瓦斯。

sentences.en: That sounds pretty terrifying to have security services come to a proteSt.
sentences.zh: 安全部队来到抗议现场听起来挺可怕的。

sentences.en: It was.
sentences.zh: 确实很可怕。

sentences.en: And every day this would happen as a routine, you would go searching for a protest, you would
sentences.zh: 每天这都成了一种例行公事，你要去找一场抗议，去

sentences.en: participate in the protest, tape the protest, and then the security services would come and crack down on it?
sentences.zh: 参加抗议，拍摄抗议，然后安全部队就会来镇压？

sentences.en: Yeah, almost every day.
sentences.zh: 对，几乎每天如此。

sentences.en: What would you say when the security services arrived?
sentences.zh: 当安全部队到达时你会说什么？

sentences.en: What would you say to them?
sentences.zh: 你对他们说什么？

sentences.en: We don't say anything.
sentences.zh: 我们什么都不说。

sentences.en: We just run.
sentences.zh: 我们只管逃跑。

sentences.en: When the security forces reach the list of the demonstrations, we know that they're going to attack, and if they're going to do helpful things, they might be firing on us.
sentences.zh: 当安全部队赶到游行示威的名单时，我们就知道他们要发起攻击了，如果他们要做点更狠的，他们甚至会向我们开火。

sentences.en: Did any of your friends get shot?
sentences.zh: 你的朋友中有人中枪吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 有的。

sentences.en: Did any of them die because of that?
sentences.zh: 他们中有人因此死亡吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 有的。

sentences.en: Some of the friends that used to participate in the demonstrations got killed by these security forces.
sentences.zh: 一些过去常参加示威活动的朋友被这些安全部队杀害了。

sentences.en: If you had to estimate how many people close to you died that way, how many would you say?
sentences.zh: 如果你估计一下有多少与你亲近的人以这种方式死去，你会说有多少？

sentences.en: Well, it's going to be a big number.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那将是一个很大的数字。

sentences.en: My estimation would be about 30.
sentences.zh: 我估计大约有30个。

sentences.en: Of 30 close friends.
sentences.zh: 30个挚友。

sentences.en: Died at the hands of the state.
sentences.zh: 死于国家之手。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Can I ask, do you consider yourself to be a rebel?
sentences.zh: 请问，你认为自己是一个叛军吗？

sentences.en: Do you consider yourself to be a member of the Free Syrian Army, or do you consider yourself to be a journalist?
sentences.zh: 你认为自己是叙利亚自由军的成员，还是认为自己是一名记者？

sentences.en: How do you consider yourself?
sentences.zh: 你怎么看你自己？

sentences.en: Well, I did not hold any guns in the past eight years.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在过去的八年里我没有拿过任何枪支。

sentences.en: I was a civilian activist, if you will.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，我是一名平民活动人士。

sentences.en: I haven't given myself any title in this matter.
sentences.zh: 我没有在这件事上给自己贴任何头衔。

sentences.en: I'm just a student who is doing what he is supposed to be doing in times like that.
sentences.zh: 我只是一名在这样的时期做着他应该做的事情的学生。

sentences.en: Did you expect that the government would come to Douma for a major attack, that it would try to completely retake the city and bombard it?
sentences.zh: 你曾预计政府会大举进攻杜马，会试图彻底收复这座城市并对其进行轰炸吗？

sentences.en: Well, the bombardment is a very obvious thing that we were expecting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，轰炸是一件很明显的事情，我们当时就预料到了。

sentences.en: We were moving in, not just expecting.
sentences.zh: 我们不仅仅是在预料。

sentences.en: It was happening.
sentences.zh: 它正在发生。

sentences.en: They just escalated the bombardment and escalated the ground assault.
sentences.zh: 他们只是升级了轰炸并升级了地面进攻。

sentences.en: I know it's so hard to look at.
sentences.zh: 我知道这太难以直视了。

sentences.en: These are the men, women, children of Douma, lying on the floor.
sentences.zh: 这些是杜马的男人、女人、儿童，躺在地板上。

sentences.en: This is an underground shelter here.
sentences.zh: 这是一个地下避难所。

sentences.en: What you see around their mouth appears to be foam.
sentences.zh: 你看到他们嘴周围似乎有泡沫。

sentences.en: That's a sign of a chemical attack.
sentences.zh: 那是化武袭击的迹象。

sentences.en: Makud, why do you think that the regime used chemical weapons on the town?
sentences.zh: 马库德，你认为政权为什么要在镇上使用化学武器？

sentences.en: After weeks of shelling, why use chemical weapons all of a sudden?
sentences.zh: 经过数周的炮击后，为什么突然使用化学武器？

sentences.en: It was the only weapon left that they did not use to bring down the city to their control.
sentences.zh: 这是他们让这座城市屈服所剩的唯一没有使用的武器了。

sentences.en: I think that they just reached the point of using something more powerful to bring the city down.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们只是到了必须使用更强大的东西来让这座城市陷落的地步。

sentences.en: That's why they used chemical weapons.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们使用化学武器的原因。

sentences.en: If you know that chemical weapons might be used, is there any precaution you can take?
sentences.zh: 如果你知道可能会使用化学武器，有什么预防措施可以采取吗？

sentences.en: Is there anything you can do?
sentences.zh: 有什么你能做的吗？

sentences.en: Or do you just have to resign yourself to the possibility that it might happen and that there's nothing you can do about it?
sentences.zh: 还是说你只能听天由命，接受它可能会发生且你对此无能为力的现实？

sentences.en: Well, because of the siege, you can't take any precautions.
sentences.zh: 嗯，由于围困，你无法采取任何预防措施。

sentences.en: The only thing that you can do is going out of the basement and up to the roof of the building.
sentences.zh: 你唯一能做的事就是离开地下室，走到大楼屋顶上去。

sentences.en: Because the chemical weapons, these gas are heavier than air.
sentences.zh: 因为化学武器，这些气体比空气重。

sentences.en: They fall down and they come into the basement.
sentences.zh: 它们会下沉并进入地下室。

sentences.en: The only thing you can do is going above and trying to get to the roof.
sentences.zh: 你唯一能做的事就是上去并设法到达屋顶。

sentences.en: But how are you supposed to do that when there is heavy shelling around you?
sentences.zh: 但周围炮火连天，你又怎么能做到这一点呢？

sentences.en: Right, you're in an impossible position.
sentences.zh: 没错，你陷入了进退维谷的境地。

sentences.en: You need to be in the basement to spare yourself from the shelling.
sentences.zh: 你需要待在地下室里以躲避炮击。

sentences.en: And that keeps you from getting up to the roof in case there's a chemical attack.
sentences.zh: 而这又阻碍了你在发生化武袭击时前往屋顶。

sentences.en: Yeah, which is the only thing you can do to protect yourself from the chemical attack.
sentences.zh: 是的，而那是保护自己免受化武袭击的唯一方法。

sentences.en: Frankly, even though it's not strange for the regime to use chemical weapons, I did not see it coming.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，尽管政权使用化学武器并不奇怪，但我还是始料未及。

sentences.en: So you were surprised that the government would take that risk?
sentences.zh: 所以你很惊讶政府会冒这个险？

sentences.en: Yeah, not because it's a strange thing for them to do, but because I did not think that the world is going to allow another chemical attack to happen again.
sentences.zh: 对，不是因为他们做出这种事很奇怪，而是因为我没想到世界会允许另一次化学袭击再次发生。

sentences.en: So what did you choose to do after the chemical attack?
sentences.zh: 那化学袭击发生后，你选择了做什么？

sentences.en: Well, I chose to leave.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我选择离开。

sentences.en: Because I don't stand the idea of having to live under the government's control.
sentences.zh: 因为我无法忍受必须在政府控制下生活的想法。

sentences.en: How did you actually leave if there was a siege around the town?
sentences.zh: 既然镇子周围被围困，你是怎么实际离开的呢？

sentences.en: How did you get out?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么出来的？

sentences.en: The deal was made between the Russians and the armed rebel groups.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人和武装反叛组织达成了一项协议。

sentences.en: The deal was to bring buses into Duma and give everyone who wants to leave the chance to leave safely.
sentences.zh: 协议是把大巴开进杜马，给所有想离开的人提供安全离开的机会。

sentences.en: That is for the civilians and for the armed rebels.
sentences.zh: 这是针对平民和武装反叛分子的。

sentences.en: And everyone who wants to stay under the government's control will have that chance, too.
sentences.zh: 所有想留在政府控制下的人也会有这个机会。

sentences.en: So you get on a bus and you leave your hometown?
sentences.zh: 所以你上了大巴，离开了你的家乡？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It was frustrating.
sentences.zh: 这让人感到沮丧。

sentences.en: It was very hard.
sentences.zh: 这非常艰难。

sentences.en: Where are you now?
sentences.zh: 你现在在哪里？

sentences.en: You're obviously in a crowded space with other families.
sentences.zh: 显然你和其它家庭在一个拥挤的空间里。

sentences.en: Where have you landed?
sentences.zh: 你落脚在哪里？

sentences.en: The buses went through the government-controlled area and into the rebel-controlled area in Aleppo suburbs.
sentences.zh: 大巴穿过了政府控制区，进入了阿勒颇郊区的反叛武装控制区。

sentences.en: The reason the room is crowded is because we are multiple families living in one apartment,
sentences.zh: 房间之所以拥挤，是因为我们多个家庭住在一套公寓里，

sentences.en: which is great circumstances if compared to the people who are in the camps.
sentences.zh: 如果跟那些在难民营里的人相比，这环境已经算很好了。

sentences.en: We saw how hard it was for the people in camps, living in tents.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了营地里住在帐篷里的人有多艰难。

sentences.en: The people who were in the same convoy and another convoy that left Duma recently.
sentences.zh: 那些人跟我们在同一支车队里，还有最近离开杜马的另一支车队。

sentences.en: Do you think that you'll ever get back to Duma?
sentences.zh: 你觉得你还会回到杜马吗？

sentences.en: That's the scariest idea that comes to my mind.
sentences.zh: 这是我脑子里最可怕的想法。

sentences.en: Scary because you want to go back and can't, or scary because if you go back, it might be destroyed?
sentences.zh: 可怕是因为你想回去却回不去，还是因为如果回去了，它可能已经被摧毁了？

sentences.en: Scary because I probably won't be able to get back.
sentences.zh: 可怕是因为我可能回不去了。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously, I can't go back to an area that is under the government's control.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很显然，我无法回到一个处于政府控制下的地区。

sentences.en: It's very risky because I'm now in the military age.
sentences.zh: 这非常冒险，因为我现在到了服兵役的年龄。

sentences.en: They might drag me to the Assad forces and have me attack other people who are in rebel-controlled areas.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会把我抓进阿萨德部队，让我去攻击其他在反叛武装控制区的人。

sentences.en: It's risky because I have civil activities that might be used against me.
sentences.zh: 这很冒险，因为我有可能会被用来作为对我不利的民事活动证据。

sentences.en: I might be taken to prisoners, I might be tortured.
sentences.zh: 我可能会被抓进监狱，我可能会遭受酷刑。

sentences.en: All of these things make me think that I won't be able to live under a government-controlled area ever.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都让我觉得我再也没法在政府控制的地区生活了。

sentences.en: It's what our streets now look like.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们现在的街道看起来的样子。

sentences.en: The situation in Duma is terrifying now.
sentences.zh: 杜马现在的局势令人恐惧。

sentences.en: What we're witnessing is a lot more horrifying than what we witnessed before.
sentences.zh: 我们正在目睹的景象比以前见过的要可怕得多。

sentences.en: But we own different things.
sentences.zh: 但我们拥有不同的东西。

sentences.en: The world is not bringing traffic and attention now to what's happening.
sentences.zh: 世界现在没有把流量和注意力放在正在发生的事情上。

sentences.en: And the reason to that is most of the photographers are out of the area now.
sentences.zh: 原因在于大多数摄影师现在都已经不在该地区了。

sentences.en: And the connections are cut off.
sentences.zh: 而且连接被切断了。

sentences.en: And it's very difficult to get what's happening out to the world.
sentences.zh: 要把这里发生的事情传达给世界非常困难。

sentences.en: So it's now everyone's job, whether you're a Syrian person or just a human being.
sentences.zh: 所以现在这是每个人的工作，无论你是叙利亚人还是仅仅作为一个人类。

sentences.en: It's now your responsibility to amplify our voices and to show the world what's happening in Duma now.
sentences.zh: 放大我们的声音、向世界展示杜马现在发生的事情，现在是你的责任。

sentences.en: We started this conversation with you describing a video that you took on the streets, the risks that you took to record that video so that the world could see what was happening.
sentences.zh: 我们开始这段对话时，你描述了你在街上拍的一段视频，为了让世界看到发生了什么，你冒着风险录下了那段视频。

sentences.en: You ended that video by saying you wanted people to do something.
sentences.zh: 你在视频结尾说，你希望人们做点什么。

sentences.en: So how does it feel now?
sentences.zh: 所以现在感觉如何？

sentences.en: It feels like a betrayal.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像是一种背叛。

sentences.en: Every step of this timeline.
sentences.zh: 这个时间线上的每一步。

sentences.en: I believed in journalism.
sentences.zh: 我曾经相信新闻业。

sentences.en: I believed in getting the world out.
sentences.zh: 我曾经相信把真相带给世界。

sentences.en: I believed in showing the suffering so it might be ended by someone who cares.
sentences.zh: 我曾相信展示苦难能让它被某个在乎的人终结。

sentences.en: When I filmed that video, that was the goal I was aiming for.
sentences.zh: 当我拍摄那段视频时，那就是我所追求的目标。

sentences.en: And I was hoping that someone would listen.
sentences.zh: 我曾希望有人会听。

sentences.en: So when a chemical attack happens, after you were demanding the world to stop the shelling, it's the exact opposite of what you were hoping the world to do.
sentences.zh: 所以当化学袭击发生时，在你要求世界停止轰炸之后，这跟你的期望完全相反。

sentences.en: It feels like a betrayal, like I said.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，感觉就像是一种背叛。

sentences.en: When you look back on when these protests started in Duma back in 2011, as part of the Arab Spring, and how hopeful that all was, that there might be change.
sentences.zh: 当你回想起2011年杜马这些抗议活动刚开始时，作为阿拉伯之春的一部分，那是多么充满希望，觉得可能会有改变。

sentences.en: And now when you realize where things are, does it seem like the rebellion was worth it?
sentences.zh: 而现在当你意识到事情的现状时，你觉得这场叛乱值得吗？

sentences.en: That it was worth trying to fight the government, given everything that's happened?
sentences.zh: 鉴于发生的一切，尝试与政府抗争是值得的吗？

sentences.en: That's kind of a hard question.
sentences.zh: 这算是个艰难的问题。

sentences.en: At that time, it wasn't being imagined that it would come to this point.
sentences.zh: 当时，人们并没有想象过事情会发展到这一步。

sentences.en: But we were hoping for a better country.
sentences.zh: 但我们曾希望能有一个更好的国家。

sentences.en: We were hoping that we'll reach a country that respects human rights.
sentences.zh: 我们曾希望我们能建立一个尊重人权的国家。

sentences.en: And because we did not achieve that goal, for me personally, that's not a reason to not do it.
sentences.zh: 而因为我们没有实现这个目标，对我个人而言，这不是不去做这件事的理由。

sentences.en: Mahmoud, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 马哈茂德，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: I know you're in a crowded room, and we've talked to you for a long time.
sentences.zh: 我知道你在一个拥挤的房间里，而且我们跟你聊了很长时间。

sentences.en: And you've been through a lot, and we're really grateful for your time and your thoughtfulness.
sentences.zh: 你经历了很多，我们非常感谢你抽出时间和深刻的见解。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: I'm happy to do it.
sentences.zh: 我很乐意。

sentences.en: Over the weekend, chemical arms inspectors said they had finally been able to visit the site of the suspected attack in Duma and collected samples for analysis.
sentences.zh: 周末时，化学武器检查人员表示，他们终于能够访问杜马疑似袭击的现场并收集了用于分析的样本。

sentences.en: The inspectors had been blocked from the site earlier in the week, raising suspicions from the West that Syria and its Russian allies, which now control Duma,
sentences.zh: 检查人员在本周早些时候曾被阻止进入现场，这引发了西方的怀疑，认为叙利亚及其俄罗斯盟友（现在控制着杜马）

sentences.en: were scrubbing the area of evidence.
sentences.zh: 在清理该区域的证据。

sentences.en: President Bashar al-Assad has denied the accusations and denied the attack itself, calling it a hoax or saying it was the rebels who used chemical weapons
sentences.zh: 巴沙尔·阿萨德总统否认了这些指控，也否认了袭击本身，称其为骗局，或者说是反叛分子使用了化学武器

sentences.en: and then blamed it on Syrian forces.
sentences.zh: 然后嫁祸给叙利亚军队。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 纽约时报应用？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁版？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费探索《时报》一个月，而且不需要输入信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你在该应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用并获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他事情。

sentences.en: The Islamic State is claiming credit for a suicide bomb that killed at least 57 people and wounded 119 more in the capital of Afghanistan on Sunday.
sentences.zh: 伊斯兰国宣称对周日在阿富汗首都发生的一起自杀式炸弹袭击负责，该袭击造成至少57人死亡、119人受伤。

sentences.en: The bomb targeted Afghans as they lined up at a government office in Kabul to register to vote.
sentences.zh: 这枚炸弹的目标是在喀布尔的一个政府办公室排队进行选民登记的阿富汗人。

sentences.en: The latest attempt by ISIS to discourage voting in upcoming legislative elections.
sentences.zh: 这是“伊斯兰国”试图阻止人们在即将到来的立法选举中投票的最新尝试。

sentences.en: Although ISIS has lost much of its land in Afghanistan after years of U.S.-led airstrikes,
sentences.zh: 尽管在美军领导的多年空袭后，“伊斯兰国”在阿富汗失去了大部分地盘，

sentences.en: it continues to try to undermine the government there with terror attacks in cities like Kabul.
sentences.zh: 但它仍继续试图通过在喀布尔等城市的恐怖袭击来破坏那里的政府。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是今天的《每日播客》。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了群自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党就陷入了一场残酷、混乱、有时又令人兴奋的争斗之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在我和萨拉·科尼格主持的最新一期《都会》节目中，讲述了人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都会》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在您获取播客的任何地方收听。
